subject: NorthStar demo — recommended engine shortlist, benchmarks & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finserv.ai>, Alex Reed <alexreed@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NorthStar demo — recommended engine shortlist, benchmarks & next steps

Samira / Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick write-up of the immediate follow-ups and our recommended engine shortlist based on the workload you shared (high-throughput batch summaries + low-latency assistant queries).

Summary of recommended shortlist (ops-ready candidates):
- redwood-lite-7B-8bit-q: Best cost profile for batch summarization (throughput) — median token cost estimate ~0.5x of larger engines, 20–30 ms per-token when batched on Dedicated capacity.
- redwood-13B-fp16: Balanced latency/quality for interactive assistant use — stronger instruction-following and fewer hallucinations in our tests, median 40–60 ms/token on the same hardware.
- open-30B-8bit: Highest quality on edge cases (legal / compliance prompts) but ~2–3x unit cost vs redwood-13B; double-check for any PII redaction SOPs before it goes live.

Key tradeoffs we observed (cost / latency / quality):
- Cost: 7B quantized variant reduces per-token spend but needs careful prompt engineering for precision-sensitive outputs.
- Latency: 13B is the middle ground; for <200ms end-to-end SLA we recommend routing short assistant queries to a warmed 13B instance with prefix caching.
- Quality: 30B improves factuality on long-context Q&A but increases cost and cold-start latency.

Included artifacts (attached): northstar_demo_benchmarks.csv (latency and token-cost traces), northstar_promptset_v1.txt (repr prompts we used), and a draft SOW for the pilot path.

Asks / next steps:
1) Samira: confirm which two intents you want prioritized for the pilot (summary batch + policy Q&A?).
2) Alex: procurement contact details so we can provision a 30-day Dedicated trial for the 13B config.
3) Internally we'll run a short regression suite focused on hallucination rates on your compliance prompt set (see attached prompt pack) and share a pass/fail guardrail.

I can do a quick 30-minute call Monday to walk through the benchmark CSV if helpful.

Thanks,
Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

1) Intent prioritization: yes — confirm we should start with (A) regulatory summary generation (batch nightly jobs) and (B) policy Q&A (interactive). That maps to your batch + assistant split.
2) Regarding redwood-lite-7B-8bit-q: are you seeing any meaningful drop in redaction/PII masking performance vs the 13B run? We have strict redaction checks we must pass before any pilot ingest.
3) Procurement: our procurement lead is Lisa Gomez (lisa.gomez@northstar.com). I can loop her in once you send a short commercial summary and pilot SOW.

Also cc'ing Alex — he flagged that our legal team will want to see a data-retention and audit-log plan for anything used in production.

Happy to take the Monday call — 11am PT works for me.

Filing a short ops note for the thread — leaving a few operational flags for the pilot path: 

- Redaction checks: we'll run the prompt pack through our PII detector and the redaction pipeline; goal is <0.1% leakage on the compliance prompt subset. If 7B fails, fallback is to run sensitive requests on the 13B instance.
- Warm pool sizing: for the interactive SLA Samira asked for, recommend a small kept-warm pool (3 x 13B) during business hours and autoscale for batch windows. I attached a quick cost delta in the CSV.
- Regression plan: propose a 2-week smoke/regression run with the NorthStar prompt set — we'll collect hallucination, factuality, and latency distributions and share a short readout.

Attachments referenced: northstar_demo_benchmarks.csv (updated with ops-level cost lines). I'll also attach a short checklist for compliance evidence we can hand to their legal team.

Markus — if you want, I can draft the pilot provisioning checklist and the runbook for the regression (will send later today).

Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finserv.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Sep 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NorthStar demo — recommended engine shortlist, benchmarks & next steps

Samira / team — quick technical addendum from our eval bench runs and suggested next steps for qualification: 

Bench highlights (short):
- redwood-lite-7B-8bit-q: batch throughput 4.8M tokens/hour on 1x pod, median summary ROUGE-L 0.62 on your sample set, hallucination rate 1.8% (above our target for compliance workloads).
- redwood-13B-fp16: throughput 2.1M tokens/hour, ROUGE-L 0.71, hallucination rate 0.6% — better fit for mixed interactive/regulatory queries.
- open-30B-8bit: throughput 0.9M tokens/hour, ROUGE-L 0.76, hallucination 0.3% — highest quality but cost and cold-start time are the tradeoffs.

Links to full artifacts: 
- Benchmark CSV (latency/cost/metrics): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2bNorthStarDemo/view
- Prompt pack used for regression: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2bNorthStarPrompts/view

Qualification recommendation: start pilot with redwood-13B-fp16 as the primary route for interactive traffic and route nightly batch summarization to redwood-lite-7B-8bit-q with a post-process QA filter that flags low-confidence outputs for re-run on 13B. If legal requires the highest fidelity on select datasets, we can enable open-30B-8bit for those jobs.

Commercial ask: we can provision a 30-day pilot on Dedicated for the 13B config — draft SOW attached (Markus, Marissa: please confirm the seat/ingest limits). Samira — once procurement (Lisa) is looped in we'll propose a commercial pilot fee and success criteria tied to hallucination and latency thresholds.

Proposed next steps (concrete):
1) Lisa Gomez from NorthStar onboarded to the thread for procurement / SOW review.
2) NorthStar confirms two pilot intents and an initial sample dataset (SFTP or shared Drive).
3) Redwood runs 2-week regression; deliverables: metrics CSV, runbook, regression readout, and a guardrail list for production blocking issues.

I'll schedule the Monday 11am PT call as a working session and share a short slide with the route decision diagram.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
